topics.title: Swimming
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list the four basic swimming strokes.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper pool safety rules.
Introduction:
We have learned about basic physical activities. Today we will focus on swimming, an important life skill that can save lives.
Content:
Swimming strokes include freestyle, breaststroke, backstroke and butterfly. Each stroke has specific arm and leg movements. For example, freestyle involves alternating arm movements while flutter kicking. Pool safety rules include no running near the pool, swimming with a buddy, and knowing the depth of each section. In Nigeria, many public pools have shallow ends for beginners.
Class activity:
Students will practice basic strokes in the shallow end while classmates provide feedback on technique.
Evaluation questions:
Name two swimming strokes.
Why is it dangerous to run near a swimming pool?
What should you do before entering deep water?
Summary:
Swimming is both a sport and a survival skill that requires knowledge of strokes and safety rules.

topics.title: Gymnastics: advanced
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to perform a handstand with proper spotting.
The students should be able to explain the safety measures for vaulting.
Introduction:
We have practiced basic gymnastics moves. Today we will advance to more complex skills like handstands and vaults.
Content:
A handstand requires strong arms, core muscles and balance. To perform one, start in a lunge position, place hands shoulder-width apart, then kick up while keeping legs straight. Vaulting involves running toward a vaulting horse, placing hands on it, and pushing off to land safely. Spotters must always be present to prevent injuries during these advanced moves.
Class activity:
Students will practice handstands against a wall with a partner spotting them, then progress to low vaults with proper supervision.
Evaluation questions:
What three body parts are most important for a good handstand?
Why is a spotter necessary for gymnastics?
Describe the proper way to approach a vaulting horse.
Summary:
Advanced gymnastics requires strength, balance and proper safety measures to prevent injuries.

topics.title: Traditional sports
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the rules of Ayo.
The students should be able to demonstrate basic wrestling techniques safely.
Introduction:
We have studied modern sports. Today we will explore traditional Nigerian sports that have been played for generations.
Content:
Ayo is a traditional board game played with seeds and a wooden board with twelve holes. Players take turns distributing seeds and capturing opponents' seeds. Traditional wrestling involves grappling techniques and strength. In Nigerian villages, wrestling matches often take place during festivals and are important cultural events. The rules emphasize skill rather than causing harm to opponents.
Class activity:
Students will play a tournament of Ayo in small groups, then practice basic wrestling stances and holds under supervision.
Evaluation questions:
How many holes are on a traditional Ayo board?
What is the purpose of capturing seeds in Ayo?
Name one cultural event where wrestling is traditionally held in Nigeria.
Summary:
Traditional sports like Ayo and wrestling are important parts of Nigerian cultural heritage that teach strategy and respect.

topics.title: Fitness training
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to design a simple fitness circuit.
The students should be able to explain the importance of progression in fitness training.
Introduction:
We have discussed the benefits of physical activity. Today we will learn how to create structured fitness plans for better results.
Content:
A fitness circuit includes different exercise stations that work various muscle groups. For example, one station might have push-ups, another jumping jacks, and another squats. Each station is performed for a set time before moving to the next. Progression means gradually increasing difficulty by adding more repetitions, time, or resistance. In Nigeria, common circuit training can be done with minimal equipment like water bottles for weights.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to design a 5-station fitness circuit that can be performed in the schoolyard.
Evaluation questions:
What are three components of a fitness circuit?
Why is progression important in fitness training?
How can household items be used in circuit training?
Summary:
Proper fitness training involves structured circuits and gradual progression to improve strength and endurance.

topics.title: Health: nutrition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list the six classes of food.
The students should be able to create a balanced meal plan for an active teenager.
Introduction:
We have learned about physical activities. Today we will explore how nutrition affects our performance and health.
Content:
The six classes of food are carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water. Carbohydrates like yam and rice provide energy, while proteins like beans and fish build muscles. An active teenager needs more calories but should still eat balanced meals. For example, a Nigerian breakfast might include akara (protein), bread (carbohydrate), and fruit (vitamins). Hydration is also crucial for performance.
Class activity:
Students will create a one-day meal plan for a student athlete using common Nigerian foods.
Evaluation questions:
Name two Nigerian foods rich in carbohydrates.
Why is water important for athletes?
What would you eat for lunch after physical education class?
Summary:
Good nutrition is essential for energy, muscle growth, and overall health, especially for active individuals.

topics.title: Health: diseases
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to differentiate between communicable and non-communicable diseases.
The students should be able to list three preventive measures for common non-communicable diseases.
Introduction:
We have studied diseases that spread from person to person. Today we will focus on non-communicable diseases that affect many Nigerians.
Content:
Non-communicable diseases are not spread from person to person and often develop over time. Common examples include hypertension, diabetes, and asthma. Hypertension, or high blood pressure, can be managed through diet, exercise, and medication. Diabetes affects how the body uses sugar and requires monitoring of blood glucose levels. Prevention includes maintaining a healthy weight, eating balanced meals, and avoiding smoking.
Class activity:
Students will create prevention posters for hypertension and diabetes using information from the lesson.
Evaluation questions:
What is the difference between communicable and non-communicable diseases?
Name two non-communicable diseases common in Nigeria.
How can diet help prevent hypertension?
Summary:
Non-communicable diseases require lifestyle changes and medical management to prevent complications.

topics.title: Health: environment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain how poor sanitation affects health.
The students should be able to suggest ways to improve environmental health in their community.
Introduction:
We have learned about personal health. Today we will explore how our environment affects our health and wellbeing.
Content:
Poor sanitation leads to diseases like cholera and typhoid that spread through contaminated water and food. In Nigeria, open defecation and improper waste disposal create health hazards. Environmental health involves keeping surroundings clean through proper waste management, clean water sources, and good drainage systems. Harmattan season brings dust that can affect respiratory health, requiring protective measures.
Class activity:
Students will design a clean-up campaign for their school compound focusing on waste segregation and proper disposal.
Evaluation questions:
Name two diseases caused by poor sanitation.
How does the harmattan season affect health?
What can students do to improve environmental health in their school?
Summary:
A clean environment is essential for preventing diseases and maintaining good health in communities.

topics.title: Recreation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list three recreational activities suitable for different age groups.
The students should be able to organize a simple recreational game session.
Introduction:
We have studied structured sports. Today we will explore recreational activities that can be enjoyed in free time for fun and relaxation.
Content:
Recreational activities include games, sports, and hobbies that people do for enjoyment. Suitable activities for children include tag, hide and seek, and simple ball games. Teenagers might enjoy football, volleyball, or board games like Ludo. Adults may prefer walking, dancing, or traditional games like Ayo. Recreation reduces stress, improves social skills, and promotes physical fitness without the pressure of competition.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to organize and lead a 15-minute recreational game session for their classmates.
Evaluation questions:
Name two recreational activities suitable for elderly people.
How does recreation benefit mental health?
What equipment is needed for a game of Ludo?
Summary:
Recreational activities provide fun, relaxation, and social interaction for people of all ages.

topics.title: Sports administration
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the process of organizing a tournament.
The students should be able to create a simple fixture for a 4-team competition.
Introduction:
We have participated in various sports. Today we will learn how to organize and manage sports events effectively.
Content:
Organizing a tournament involves several steps: planning the event, setting rules, creating fixtures, and arranging officials. Fixtures show which teams play against each other at different times. For example, in a 4-team football tournament, each team plays every other team once. Rules must be clear and fair to all participants. In Nigeria, tournaments often use local venues and volunteers to reduce costs while maintaining quality.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to organize a mini-football tournament for their class, including rules, fixtures, and equipment lists.
Evaluation questions:
What are three important steps in organizing a tournament?
How does a fixture help in tournament organization?
Why are clear rules important in sports competitions?
Summary:
Proper sports administration ensures fair, organized, and enjoyable competitions for all participants.

topics.title: Revision and BECE practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to solve past BECE questions on physical and health education.
The students should be able to identify common mistakes in answering exam questions.
Introduction:
We have covered many topics this term. Today we will revise key concepts and practice answering examination questions.
Content:
Revision involves reviewing important topics like swimming strokes, fitness training, nutrition, and sports administration. Past BECE questions help students understand the format and types of questions they may encounter. Common mistakes include not reading questions carefully, not providing complete answers, and not managing time properly. Students should practice answering questions under timed conditions to build confidence.
Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to answer past BECE questions, then swap papers to mark and provide feedback.
Evaluation questions:
Name two components of fitness training.
Why is nutrition important for athletes?
How should you prepare for a physical education examination?
Summary:
Regular practice with past questions helps students improve their exam techniques and knowledge retention.
